title: test: assert the `initialized` event on initialize
body:
### Context

`initialize` publishes an `Initialized` event (topic `initialized`, data `{ admin, anchor, token }`), but no test checks it. Indexers rely on it to discover new deployments.

### Scope

**Files:** `contracts/escrow/src/test/flows.rs`

Add a test that calls `initialize` on an uninitialised contract (`Setup::uninitialized()`) and compares `env.events().all().filter_by_contract(...)` with `Initialized { .. }.to_xdr(...)`. Capture events **immediately** after the call: `events().all()` only holds the most recent invocation's events. Follow the pattern in `deposit_locks_funds_and_emits_locked`.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new test asserts the exact `initialized` event, topics and data
- [ ] The test fails if a field of the event is changed
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `stellar contract build && cargo test` pass

### Complexity

Trivial (100 points)

title: docs: document how to compute tx_id, with test vectors
body:
### Context

The escrow is keyed by `tx_id = sha256(utf8(zephyr transaction uuid))`. The backend, frontend and CLI users all have to compute it identically, or deposits won't match their withdrawals.

### Scope

**Files:** `docs/tx-id.md (new)`, `README.md`

Write `docs/tx-id.md` showing how to compute the `tx_id` in TypeScript (Web Crypto `crypto.subtle.digest` and Node `crypto`), Rust (`sha2` or `env.crypto().sha256`) and shell (`printf '%s' | sha256sum`, with no trailing newline). Include at least three UUID → hex test vectors, and link the page from the README.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/tx-id.md` has TS, Rust and shell examples
- [ ] At least three test vectors, each checked by running the shell example
- [ ] The page explains the trailing-newline pitfall
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `stellar contract build && cargo test` pass

### Complexity

Trivial (100 points)

title: ci: fail when committed bindings don't match the contract interface
body:
### Context

`bindings/` is committed so that the backend and frontend can consume `@zephyr-ramp/escrow-client` without Rust. If someone changes the contract interface and forgets `./scripts/bindings.sh`, the published client silently drifts from the contract.

### Scope

**Files:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `scripts/bindings.sh`

Add a CI job that builds the wasm, regenerates bindings with `LOCAL_ONLY=1` into a temp directory, and diffs `src/index.ts` against the committed one. body:

title: feat(escrow): public extend_ttl(tx_id) so anyone can keep an escrow alive
body:
### Context

An escrow's TTL is extended on every write, to `expires_ledger + 30 days`. If a user forgets to refund for longer than that, the entry is archived and needs a manual `restore`. A permissionless bump lets a wallet or keeper keep it live.

### Scope

**Files:** `contracts/escrow/src/lib.rs`, `contracts/escrow/src/storage.rs`, `contracts/escrow/src/test/`

Add `extend_ttl(tx_id)`, with no auth, which re-applies the TTL policy from `storage::write_escrow` without changing data. Return `NotFound` for unknown IDs. Factor the TTL computation so it isn't duplicated.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test shows the TTL increases after advancing ledgers and calling `extend_ttl`
- [ ] Escrow data is unchanged
- [ ] No auth required (asserted with `env.auths()` being empty)
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `stellar contract build && cargo test` pass

### Complexity

Medium (150 points)

title: feat(escrow): two-step admin transfer (propose_admin / accept_admin)
body:
### Context

There's no way to rotate the admin key. Before mainnet the admin must move to a multisig, and a one-step `set_admin` risks bricking admin control with a typo. A two-step transfer requires the new admin to prove control.

### Scope

**Files:** `contracts/escrow/src/lib.rs`, `contracts/escrow/src/types.rs`, `contracts/escrow/src/events.rs`, `contracts/escrow/src/test/admin.rs`, `README.md`

Add `propose_admin(new_admin)` (admin auth), which stores a pending admin, and `accept_admin()` (pending admin's auth), which makes it the admin and clears the pending entry. Emit `admin_proposed` and `admin_changed`. Calling `accept_admin` with nothing pending returns a new error `NoPendingAdmin`.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Old admin keeps control until acceptance
- [ ] Only the proposed address can accept
- [ ] Proposing again replaces the pending admin
- [ ] Auth, event and error tests; README updated; bindings regenerated
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `stellar contract build && cargo test` pass

### Complexity

title: feat(escrow)!: replace initialize with __constructor
body:
### Context

`initialize` runs in a separate transaction after deploy, so someone watching the network could initialise first with their own admin. `deploy-testnet.sh` detects this and aborts, but a constructor removes the window entirely: soroban-sdk supports `__constructor`, which runs atomically at deploy.

### Scope

**Files:** `contracts/escrow/src/lib.rs`, `contracts/escrow/src/error.rs`, `contracts/escrow/src/test/`, `scripts/deploy-testnet.sh`, `README.md`, `bindings/`

Move initialisation into `__constructor(admin, anchor, token, min_timeout, max_timeout)` and remove `initialize`. Keep `AlreadyInitialized`/`NotInitialized` in the error enum (codes must stay stable); document them as reserved. Update the test `Setup` to pass constructor args to `env.register`, update the deploy script to pass args to `stellar contract deploy -- ...`, regenerate bindings, and update the README (functions, threat model, roadmap). Coordinate with the backend and frontend maintainers in the PR.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The contract cannot exist uninitialised
- [ ] Invalid constructor args make deployment fail
- [ ] All existing tests are ported and pass
- [ ] Deploy script and README updated; a fresh testnet deployment is recorded in `deployments/testnet.json`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `stellar contract build && cargo test` pass

### Complexity

High (200 points)

title: feat(escrow): timelocked upgrades so users can exit before code changes
body:
### Context

A compromised admin key can `upgrade` to malicious code and take every escrowed fund. This is the biggest trust assumption in the threat model. A timelock gives users time to see a pending upgrade and refund before it applies.

### Scope

**Files:** `contracts/escrow/src/lib.rs`, `contracts/escrow/src/types.rs`, `contracts/escrow/src/events.rs`, `contracts/escrow/src/test/`, `README.md`

Replace `upgrade` with `schedule_upgrade(wasm_hash)` (admin), which records the hash and `ready_ledger = now + UPGRADE_DELAY`, where the delay must be longer than `max_timeout_ledgers`; `cancel_upgrade()` (admin); and `apply_upgrade()` (anyone, only at or after `ready_ledger`). Emit events for each. Add `get_pending_upgrade()`. Decide, and document, how `set_timeouts` interacts with a pending upgrade.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Upgrade can't apply before the delay (boundary tests at -1/0/+1)
- [ ] Every escrow locked before scheduling can reach expiry and refund before the upgrade applies (test)
- [ ] Threat model section updated
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `stellar contract build && cargo test` pass

### Complexity

High (200 points)

title: feat(escrow): claim_many for high-volume anchors
body:
### Context

The anchor claims each escrow in its own transaction. At volume, that means many fees and a lot of RPC traffic. A batch claim cuts both, but its failure semantics need care.

### Scope

**Files:** `contracts/escrow/src/lib.rs`, `contracts/escrow/src/test/`, `README.md`, `bindings/`

Add `claim_many(tx_ids: Vec<BytesN<32>>) -> Vec<Result-like status>` (anchor auth, once). Choose and document **one** semantics: all-or-nothing, or skip-and-report (return a per-ID outcome code). Make a single token transfer for the total. Enforce a max batch size, and measure resource usage for batches of 1, 10 and the max.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Semantics documented in README and doc comments
- [ ] Tests: all valid; some expired, not locked or unknown; duplicate IDs within one batch; over the cap
- [ ] The balance-invariant property test includes `claim_many`
- [ ] Resource usage for batch sizes recorded in the PR
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `stellar contract build && cargo test` pass

title: Commission an external security audit of the escrow contract
body:
### Context

The escrow holds user funds and is **unaudited**. The README and SECURITY.md state that Zephyr must not be used with real funds until an external audit is complete.

### Scope

- Freeze an audit commit, and tag it `audit-v1`
- Prepare an audit package: README threat model, function/error/event tables, test report and the property-test description
- Engage an auditor with Soroban experience
- Track findings as private advisories; fix and re-verify
- Publish the report in `audits/` and link it from the README

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Audit report published in `audits/`
- [ ] All critical and high findings fixed or formally accepted with rationale
- [ ] README "unaudited" warning updated to reference the audited commit

_Maintainer-led; not a Drips Wave task._
